questions.question: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'CAPRICIOUS'.
questions.title: Opposite of CAPRICIOUS

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Capricious = impulsive, unpredictable, given to sudden changes of mood/behavior.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Steadfast / Consistent** (the opposite of unpredictable is dependable/steady).

questions.question: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to the word 'INTRANSIGENT'.
questions.title: Similar to INTRANSIGENT

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Intransigent = refusing to change one's views or agree about something; uncompromising.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Stubborn / Unyielding.**

questions.question: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to the advanced vocabulary word 'LASSITUDE'.
questions.title: Similar to LASSITUDE

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Lassitude = a state of physical or mental weariness; lack of energy.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Fatigue / Lethargy.**

questions.question: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'ALACRITY'.
questions.title: Opposite of ALACRITY

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Alacrity = brisk and cheerful readiness/eagerness.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Reluctance / Sluggishness.**

questions.question: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to the word 'MITIGATE'.
questions.title: Similar to MITIGATE

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Mitigate = to make less severe, serious, or painful.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Alleviate / Lessen.**

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom: "To rest on one's laurels"?
questions.title: Idiom: "To rest on one's laurels"
options: To be satisfied with past success and stop trying to achieve more
To win a prize in a race
questions.answer: To be satisfied with past success and stop trying to achieve more

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: It means **to be so satisfied with past achievements/success that one stops making further effort to improve or achieve more** — coasting on old accomplishments instead of striving further.

questions.question: Complete the analogy: CACOPHONY : EUPHONY :: ?
questions.title: Analogy: CACOPHONY : EUPHONY :: ?

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: CACOPHONY (harsh, discordant sound) and EUPHONY (pleasant, harmonious sound) are direct **antonyms**.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: The relationship is antonymous — a matching pair would be something like **DISCORD : HARMONY** (harsh disagreement vs. pleasant agreement), i.e., look for a word pair that is likewise a pair of opposites.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Please abstain ___ smoking in the hospital premises.
questions.title: Fill in the blank: "Please abstain ___ smoking"

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"abstain FROM smoking"** — the verb "abstain" is idiomatically followed by the preposition "from."

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Neither the manager nor the employees ____ present at the meeting today.
questions.title: "Neither the manager nor the employees ____ present"

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the subject **closer to it** (here, "employees," which is plural).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"...are present..."**

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom: "To smell a rat"?
questions.title: Idiom: "To smell a rat"
options: To suspect that something is wrong or dishonest
questions.answer: To suspect that something is wrong or dishonest

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: It means **to suspect that something is wrong, dishonest, or deceptive is happening**, even without direct proof.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She showed great ___ in handling the delicate diplomatic crisis without causing offense.
questions.title: Fill in the blank: "She showed great ___ in handling the diplomatic crisis..."

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"tact"** — the ability to handle sensitive matters without giving offense.

questions.question: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to the word 'FASTIDIOUS'.
questions.title: Similar to FASTIDIOUS

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Fastidious = very attentive to and concerned about accuracy/detail; excessively particular.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Meticulous / Fussy.**

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She congratulated him ___ his success.
questions.title: Fill in the blank: "She congratulated him ___ his success."

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"...congratulated him ON his success"** — "congratulate" idiomatically takes "on."

questions.question: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to the word 'ZENITH'.
questions.title: Similar to ZENITH

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Zenith = the highest point reached; the peak.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Peak / Apex / Summit.**

questions.question: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'TRANSPARENT'.
questions.title: Opposite of TRANSPARENT

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Opaque.**

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Not only the committee members but also the chairman _____ expressing grave concerns regarding the recently proposed corporate merger.
questions.title: "Not only the committee members but also the chairman _____ expressing concerns"

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: With "not only...but also," the verb agrees with the subject **nearer to it** — here, "the chairman" (singular).

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"...is expressing grave concerns..."**

questions.question: What is the traditional meaning of the literary idiom: "Sword of Damocles"?
questions.title: Idiom: "Sword of Damocles"
options: A constant looming danger despite apparent security
questions.answer: A constant looming danger despite apparent security

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: It refers to **an impending sense of doom or constant danger/threat lurking despite an outward appearance of security and prosperity** (from the legend of Damocles seated under a sword hung by a single hair).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The defense attorney was able to mathematically corroborate his client's alibi, effectively _____ the prosecutor's timeline of the crime.
questions.title: Fill in the blank: "...effectively _____ the prosecutor's timeline..."

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Corroborating the alibi means undermining/disproving the opposing timeline.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"...effectively REFUTING (or invalidating/contradicting) the prosecutor's timeline..."**

questions.question: Complete the analogy: EPHEMERAL is to ENDURING as ILLUSORY is to:
questions.title: Analogy: EPHEMERAL : ENDURING :: ILLUSORY : ?

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: EPHEMERAL (short-lived) and ENDURING (long-lasting) are antonyms.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: ILLUSORY (not real/deceptive appearance) is to **REAL / GENUINE** — its antonym.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom: "To bury the hatchet"?
questions.title: Idiom: "To bury the hatchet"
options: To make peace after a conflict
questions.answer: To make peace after a conflict

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: It means **to make peace and end a conflict or disagreement** (originating from a Native American custom of literally burying tomahawks to signal a truce).

questions.question: Choose the correct one-word substitution for: "A person who completely abstains from alcoholic drinks".
questions.title: One-word substitution: "A person who completely abstains from alcoholic drinks"

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Teetotaler.**

questions.question: What is the contextual meaning of the historical idiom: "A Pyrrhic victory"?
questions.title: Idiom: "A Pyrrhic victory"
options: A victory won at too great a cost
questions.answer: A victory won at too great a cost

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: It refers to **a victory won at such a devastating cost (in resources, casualties, or effort) that it is nearly equivalent to a defeat** — the victor is so weakened that "winning" brings little real benefit.

questions.question: Choose the correct one-word substitution for: "A general pardon for offenses, especially political offenses, granted by a government."
questions.title: One-word substitution: "A general pardon for offenses, especially political offenses, granted by a government"

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Amnesty.**

questions.question: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to the word 'DERISION'.
questions.title: Similar to DERISION

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Derision = contemptuous ridicule or mockery.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Mockery / Ridicule / Scorn.**

questions.question: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'ENERVATE'.
questions.title: Opposite of ENERVATE

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Enervate = to weaken or drain of energy/vitality.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Invigorate / Energize.**

questions.question: Complete the analogy: ANESTHETIC is to PAIN as PACIFIER is to:
questions.title: Analogy: ANESTHETIC : PAIN :: PACIFIER : ?

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: An anesthetic is used to eliminate/suppress pain; similarly, a pacifier is used to soothe/quiet something.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: PACIFIER is to **CRYING (or distress/irritation)** — the thing it is meant to calm or eliminate.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Scarcely had he left the room ____ it started raining heavily.
questions.title: Fill in the blank: "Scarcely had he left the room ____ it started raining..."

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: "Scarcely had...when" is the standard fixed inversion construction (not "than" or "that").

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"Scarcely had he left the room WHEN it started raining heavily."**

questions.question: Choose the word that is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to the word 'PRODIGAL'.
questions.title: Opposite of PRODIGAL

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Prodigal = wastefully extravagant; spending resources recklessly.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Frugal / Thrifty.**

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He is addicted ___ smoking.
questions.title: Fill in the blank: "He is addicted ___ smoking."

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"addicted TO smoking"** — "addicted" idiomatically takes "to."

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Scarcely had I reached the railway station ___ the train departed.
questions.title: Fill in the blank: "Scarcely had I reached the railway station ___ the train departed."

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"...reached the railway station WHEN the train departed."** (same "scarcely...when" construction as Q27).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: One of my friends ___ going to Japan.
questions.title: Fill in the blank: "One of my friends ___ going to Japan."

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: "One of my friends" — the subject of the verb is "one" (singular), not "friends."

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"One of my friends IS going to Japan."**

questions.question: Similar to word 'BENEVOLENT'
questions.title: Similar to word 'BENEVOLENT'

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Benevolent = well-meaning, kindly, generous in nature.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Kind / Generous.**

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The manager insisted ___ completing the report by Friday.'
questions.title: Fill in the blank: 'The manager insisted ___ completing the

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: 'Insist' idiomatically pairs with the preposition 'on' when followed by a gerund/noun phrase describing what is being insisted upon.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **"...insisted ON completing the report by Friday."**

questions.question: Idiom: 'To let the cat out of the bag'
questions.title: Idiom: 'To let the cat out of the bag'
options: To escape from a difficult situation

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: A classic idiom about secrecy.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: It means **to accidentally or carelessly reveal a secret or piece of confidential information.**
